name: Claw Code
pass5_evidence: 'Claw Code is the public Rust implementation of the claw CLI agent harness.' Buildable from source; claw prompt / interactive sessions, own tools, skills, provider routing, doctor check.
lifecycle_finding: ADDITION: the README's own top banner says 'Claw Code is not the serious production project here ... closer to a museum exhibit than a product pitch', an 'agent-managed exhibit', and points users to LazyCodex or Gajae-Code to actually run work. Upstream the binary was RENAMED to agent-code - the claw-code crate on crates.io is a deprecated stub that only prints 'claw-code has been renamed to agent-code'.
review_flag: Capability is genuinely harness, but pass 4 missed the rename and the explicit non-production positioning. The 195k star count is disproportionate to a self-declared exhibit.

name: DeerFlow
pass5_evidence: DeerFlow 2.0 is 'an open-source super agent harness that orchestrates sub-agents, memory, and sandboxes'; setup wizard configures sandbox mode, bash access and file-write tools, so it owns a loop that can create and modify files.
lifecycle_finding: 2.0 is a ground-up rewrite sharing no code with v1; the original Deep Research framework lives on the 1.x branch.
review_flag: RULED BR-007 (2026-08-25): stays harness - it ships a documented software-engineering surface (sandbox, bash access, file-write tools, repository tasks) and self-describes as a harness. Optional ACP delegation to mcode is additive, not a substitute for its own loop.

name: MetaGPT
pass5_evidence: Ships a runnable product, not just a library: 'metagpt "Create a 2048 game"  # this will create a repo in ./workspace'. One-line requirement drives its own PM/architect/engineer SOP pipeline that writes a repository.
lifecycle_finding: Repo last push 2026-01-21; commercial successor is MGX (mgx.dev).
review_flag: This is the clean line separating it from CrewAI/AutoGen/Swarms (support): MetaGPT ships a default end-to-end coding application, they do not.

name: AutoGen
pass5_evidence: Framework for developers to build multi-agent systems. Magentic-One offers a MagenticOne helper class with minimal configuration, but it remains part of AutoGen's framework approach and is a generalist web/file task system, not a shipped project-coding product.

name: CrewAI
pass5_evidence: Self-described 'Framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents'. Developers define roles, tasks, tools and flow logic; no built-in coding product takes a repo task.

name: GPT Engineer
pass5_evidence: The gpte CLI owns generation and improvement, writes and executes code, and can modify an existing project from a prompt.
lifecycle_finding: Repository ARCHIVED (read-only), last push 2025-05-14. Precursor to Lovable.

name: ChatDev
pass5_evidence: Current named product is ChatDev 2.0 / DevAll: a 'Zero-Code Multi-Agent Platform' where users configure agents and workflows for arbitrary scenarios (data visualisation, 3D generation, deep research). The software-company harness is ChatDev 1.0, preserved on the chatdev1.0 branch.
lifecycle_finding: ChatDev 2.0 released 2026-01-07; 1.0 moved to a legacy branch.
review_flag: RESOLVED BR-008 (2026-08-25): no-code agent-building platforms are support. Coze Studio moved to support to match; both now sit with the other agent frameworks.

name: AgentScope
pass5_evidence: Agent/tool framework supplying ReAct agents, a toolkit and shell/file functions for developers to compose applications. No shipped project-coding workflow.

name: Roo Code CLI
pass5_evidence: Roo Code's own agent modes generated, refactored, debugged and edited files through an agentic loop; it was not a controller for another agent.
lifecycle_finding: DISCONTINUED: shutdown announced 2026-04-21; repository archived 2026-05-15 and read-only; team pivoted entirely to Roomote (roomote.dev), a Slack-first cloud agent. Community successors: Zoo Code (official handoff) and Kilo Code. roocodeinc.github.io now 404s.
review_flag: Historical classification only.

name: Prime Agent
pass5_evidence: Standalone agent: persistent IPython control environment where 'file operations, shell commands, tool use, subagents, and context management happen through code'; rlm(...) spawns internal child agents; daemon-backed sessions survive terminal disconnects.

name: Qwen-Agent
pass5_evidence: Self-described 'Agent framework and applications built upon Qwen' with function calling, MCP, code interpreter and RAG. Developers assemble the agent and tools.

name: Dagger
pass5_evidence: Official docs confirm there is 'no built-in, ready-to-run coding agent shipped with Dagger'; developers author the agent as a Dagger Function while Dagger supplies the tool-use framework and execution environment.

name: Aperant
pass5_evidence: README Requirements section is decisive: 'Claude Pro/Max subscription' and 'Claude Code CLI - npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code'. Aperant plans, opens worktrees and coordinates planner/coder/QA sessions; Claude Code owns the coding loops.
lifecycle_finding: Formerly Auto Claude. 2.x is in maintenance mode; 3.0 is being rebuilt in a separate repo, PRs paused, no release date.

name: Claurst
pass5_evidence: 'Open-source, multi-provider terminal coding agent built from the ground up in Rust', a clean-room reimplementation of Claude Code behaviour with its own core agent, provider routing, TUI, plugins and /goal multi-turn objectives. Does not run Claude Code.

name: Codex Security
pass5_evidence: OpenAI's own AGENTS.md in the repo states: 'Codex Security is a thin wrapper around Codex and its security plugin.' Patching is delegated - 'Each selected finding runs in its own saved Codex desktop task'. Its own scan loop is agentic, but the code-changing capability (--patch/--create-pr) is exactly the part Codex performs.
review_flag: RESOLVED BR-009 (2026-08-25): wrappers are multiplexer when the code-changing step is delegated; neither 'single agent' nor 'first-party' is material. Consistent with opcode and Aperant, which wrap Claude Code alone and are multiplexers. BR-001 does not reach it: the named unit is a scanning product that ships an SDK, not an SDK. Contrast with deepsec (support): deepsec calls raw model APIs and never modifies code, so it stays support; Codex Security modifies code but only by dispatching Codex, so it lands multiplexer rather than harness.

name: PraisonAI
pass5_evidence: Framework/SDK ecosystem (core SDK, CLI, dashboard, flow builder, UI) for developer-defined agents. Official docs confirm it is 'primarily a framework/SDK, not a pre-built coding agent'; the CLI is a deployment/orchestration layer that executes agents you define. No shipped agent that takes a repo task and edits files.
review_flag: CHANGE harness->support. Same class as CrewAI/AutoGen/Swarms/AgentScope/Qwen-Agent, all already support. Pass 4's own lifecycle note ('framework and CLI ecosystem') contradicted its harness label.

name: Flue
pass5_evidence: 'Flue - The Agent Harness Framework. Not another SDK. Build autonomous agents with Flue's programmable TypeScript harness.' The developer writes the agent function and composes model, sandbox, skills and tools; Flue ships no ready-made coding agent.

name: Claude Agent SDK (Python)
pass5_evidence: Named unit is an SDK, and per the census ruling that all SDKs are support, it classifies as support. Substantively it is developer infrastructure: the application a developer ships is theirs, and the SDK bundles the Claude Code CLI as the runtime that executes the loop.
review_flag: RESOLVED BY POLICY 2026-08-24: census owner ruled all SDKs belong in support. Supersedes the pass-4/pass-5 multiplexer reading, which applied the functional 'runs a complete coding loop' disqualifier over the nominal SDK listing. Now consistent with Strands Agents SDK, LangChain JS Tools and TypeChat.

name: Sweep
pass5_evidence: The JetBrains Sweep Agent 'automatically searches your codebase, edits your code, and then runs tests / checks for linter errors', handling multi-file changes on its own models.
lifecycle_finding: Identity shifted from the original GitHub issue-to-PR bot to a JetBrains-first IDE agent; ~40k installs. VS Code/Zed get autocomplete only.

name: Swarms
pass5_evidence: Self-described 'Enterprise-Grade Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework'. Provides Agent loops and tool/MCP integration; the developer supplies agent, prompts and tools.

name: GPT Migrate
pass5_evidence: Runnable migration workflow: recursively analyses a source codebase, writes the target codebase, creates tests, executes them in Docker and performs GPT-assisted debugging.

name: Strands Agents SDK
pass5_evidence: An SDK supplying an agent loop and tool interfaces; agents are developer-constructed on top of the core infrastructure. No shipped repository-editing product.

name: Google AI Studio Build
pass5_evidence: Build mode generates a complete client+server application from a prompt; 'The agent will automatically identify and install packages as needed for your app', manages dependencies across multiple files, retains file state across prompts, and the Antigravity Agent performs 'Verified execution: Verifies code updates to reduce hallucinations'.

name: Google Opal
pass5_evidence: No-code platform for AI mini-apps: 'Build, edit and share mini-AI apps using natural language', chaining prompts, model calls and tools into hosted visual workflows. Google hosts the mini-apps and the user does not receive a codebase.

name: AWS Transform
pass5_evidence: Ships task-specific agents that analyse source assets, plan modernisation, transform application/code artifacts, test results and can merge or deploy after human approval. Owns those transformation jobs.

name: Rovo Dev
pass5_evidence: Atlassian's terminal coding agent for natural-language development tasks - generating, refactoring, debugging, testing and reviewing code - with its own tools, subagents, sessions and worktree mode.

name: Agentforce for Developers
pass5_evidence: Current product is Agentforce Vibes with the Vibe Codey agent - context-aware, understands org metadata, and 'execute[s] on your behalf', creating and modifying Apex/LWC/trigger/test files.
lifecycle_finding: Name has drifted: the Einstein/Agentforce for Developers guide is marked Deprecated in Salesforce docs. Vibes launched Oct 2025; Vibes 2.0 unveiled at TDX 2026 as the successor to Code Builder, launchable from Setup.

name: Databricks Assistant
pass5_evidence: Current identity is Genie Code: it 'generates and runs code, builds pipelines and AI/BI dashboards, debugs errors' and 'handles multi-step tasks autonomously' across notebooks, SQL editor, pipelines and dashboards.
lifecycle_finding: Active under Genie Code branding (Genie family: Genie Code, Genie One, Genie Agents).

name: Doubao MarsCode
pass5_evidence: Renamed to Trae Plugin; Builder Mode autonomously decomposes requirements and completes multi-step coding tasks in supported IDEs, positioning the product as an 'AI Engineer' rather than an assistant.
lifecycle_finding: Rebranded MarsCode -> Trae Plugin on 2025-04-16; SOLO Mode shipped Nov 2025; marscode.com now serves Trae.

name: iFlow CLI
pass5_evidence: Terminal agent with its own planning/task tools, permission modes, repository analysis, file modification, shell execution and subagents.
lifecycle_finding: DISCONTINUED: iFlow CLI stopped updates and closed 2026-04-17 (UTC+8); the team consolidated its AI programming resources and directed users to Qoder for migration. The vibex.iflow.cn community site is still up.
review_flag: Historical classification only.

name: Baidu Comate
pass5_evidence: Comate AI IDE Mission Mode takes over the full task process: the user states a goal and the agent works against the project workspace, advances tasks and presents code changes. Owned loop with project-file access.

name: MiniMax Agent
pass5_evidence: A 'general intelligent agent designed to tackle long-horizon, complex tasks'. Official material shows it generating standalone artifacts - product pages, an online Louvre in 3 minutes, tutorials with audio narration - not editing files in an existing project or repository. MiniMax's own tagline is 'Code is cheap, show me the requirement'.
lifecycle_finding: code.minimax.io now 302s to agent.minimax.io, so the coding web surface has been folded into the general agent; the mcode CLI still exists and DeerFlow invokes it via ACP for 'implementation, refactoring, debugging, and repository tasks'.
review_flag: RULED BR-007 (2026-08-25): general-purpose agent that can code, with no documented surface operating on an existing codebase, so something-else. COVERAGE GAP: MiniMax Code / mcode is a distinct coding unit and warrants its own census row as a harness - it is not in the first 100.

name: Youware
pass5_evidence: Official homepage advertises a 'dedicated web app agent team', 'the most advanced coding agents', and an error fixer that 'Automatically test and resolve issues'. It generates a full editable codebase, builds databases, and iterates with project context. That is an owned plan-act-test-repair loop that creates and modifies code.
review_flag: REVERT support->harness (restores original label). Pass 4 claimed 'no documented autonomous plan-act-test-repair loop'; the product homepage documents exactly that. 'support' is also definitionally wrong: YouWare is not spec/prompt/context/memory/SDK/framework/workflow support.

name: Trickle
pass5_evidence: Magic Canvas is 'the first agentic canvas for AI collaboration': it generates, refines and expands multi-page apps in real time, infers rules, defines database collections, and 'all edits are instantly converted into production-grade code'.

name: Blitzy
pass5_evidence: Ingests a repository, produces an Agent Action Plan with file-level changes, generates code, compiles and tests in isolated environments, refines, and opens a pull request. Owns the task-to-PR loop.
lifecycle_finding: Active (docs behind bot protection but reachable in a browser).

name: Charlie Labs
pass5_evidence: Takes an assigned issue or natural-language request, creates a branch, implements the fix, commits, opens a PR, reviews code and responds to requested changes on its own PRs.

name: Gitar
pass5_evidence: AI code-review and CI-fixing agent: reads diffs, files, CI logs and repo rules, diagnoses failures, pushes fix commits, observes the next CI result and iterates until CI passes. Narrow but complete owned loop that modifies code.

name: Solver
pass5_evidence: Solver (formerly Laredo Labs) builds 'agents to manage repositories and carry out end-to-end software development tasks'; it 'completes repository-level tasks from natural instructions'. GitHub org bio: 'Building the future of software engineering.' This is an owned repository-level coding loop.
lifecycle_finding: MATERIAL: acquired by Nvidia. Product docs domain docs.api.solverai.com no longer resolves; solver.dev does not resolve. Org blog now solverai.com.
review_flag: REVERT support->harness (restores original label). Pass 4 derived 'support' from a 1-star, description-less SDK repo (Laredo-Labs/solverai-sdk-python, last push 2025-07-25) rather than the product, and missed the acquisition entirely.

name: Ona
pass5_evidence: Official docs: 'Codex Agent runs the open-source Codex harness in an Ona environment with your project context, environment isolation, integrations, and guardrails.' Ona supplies environments, runners, guardrails and parallel sessions; the chosen harness does the coding.
lifecycle_finding: CORRECTION: OpenAI's acquisition of Ona (ex-Gitpod, 79 people) was ANNOUNCED 2026-06-11 and, as of mid-August 2026, remained subject to closing conditions and regulatory approval with no confirmed close date.
review_flag: Pass 4 stated the acquisition 'closed ... on August 10, 2026'. No source supports a completed close; the deal was still pending.

name: Code Metal
pass5_evidence: Agentic workflow that analyses source and dependencies, generates a transpilation/deployment plan, produces target code (C/C++/Rust/VHDL/Verilog/CUDA), builds variants, validates semantic behaviour and automatically retries generation.
review_flag: Evidence is vendor product marketing rather than technical documentation.

name: Fume
pass5_evidence: Repository-connected coding product: users select a processed GitHub/GitLab repo and give implementation, debugging, UI-change or feature tasks; Fume implements the changes in that codebase.
review_flag: Single official docs source.

name: Bismuth
pass5_evidence: Coding agent that imports or creates projects, plans tasks, writes code, analyses and corrects its own mistakes, updates dependencies, proposes git commits and can take GitHub issues.
review_flag: Primary source is a Webflow product page rather than technical docs.

name: Pythagora
pass5_evidence: GPT Pilot / Pythagora is an AI developer that plans, writes, reviews, debugs and runs commands to build an app end to end - an owned coding loop.
lifecycle_finding: MATERIAL, MISSED BY PASS 4: (1) the gpt-pilot repo carries a security notice - a Shai-Hulud-class supply-chain worm (credential stealer) sat in core/telemetry/ from Aug 2025 until it was removed 2026-06-11; (2) the repo states it is 'no longer actively maintained'; (3) the company rebranded - pythagora.ai now redirects to pazi.ai, and Pazi (launched on Product Hunt 2026-07-28) is a platform for building autonomous companies from business-role agents, not a coding harness.
review_flag: Pass 4 described a 'current Pythagora product snapshot' as an active VS Code/Cursor AI teammate. The coding product is superseded and unmaintained, and the repo has an active security advisory.

name: claude-flow
pass5_evidence: Now Ruflo: 'The original agent meta-harness' - routing, swarms, memory, hooks, goals, worktrees and autonomous outer loops layered around Claude Code and Codex, which own the coding loops.

name: Orca
pass5_evidence: 'The ADE for working with a fleet of parallel agents. Run any coding agent with your own subscription.' Launches Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and others in isolated git worktrees and fans prompts across them.

name: oh-my-claudecode
pass5_evidence: Self-described 'Teams-first Multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code'. Its terminal runtime launches real Claude Code, Codex or Gemini workers in tmux.
lifecycle_finding: Active. Note owner casing is Yeachan-Heo.

name: cmux
pass5_evidence: Ghostty-based terminal for running many coding agents: creates and restores workspaces/panes, surfaces notifications, renders subagents, while Claude Code, Codex and others do the work.

name: Archon
pass5_evidence: 'A workflow engine for AI coding agents' - YAML workflows define plan/implement/validate/review/PR phases and run in isolated worktrees. Prerequisites include Claude Code ('don't bundle Claude Code. Install it separately, then point Archon at it'); the architecture diagram routes an Executor to Claude / Codex / Pi.
lifecycle_finding: Original Python task-management + RAG version archived on the archive/v1-task-management-rag branch.
review_flag: The 'harness builder' tagline is marketing; the executor is an external coding agent.

name: opcode
pass5_evidence: GUI/toolkit for Claude Code: creates custom agents, manages interactive Claude Code sessions, runs background agents. Claude Code is the worker and session substrate.
lifecycle_finding: CORRECTION: NOT active. Last commit 2025-10-13, pushed_at 2025-10-16, 331 open issues - roughly ten months dormant as of 2026-08-24.
review_flag: Pass 4 asserted 'Active repository with current commits and open development'. That is factually wrong per the GitHub API.

name: ralph
pass5_evidence: 'An autonomous AI agent loop that runs repeatedly until all PRD items are complete' - it repeatedly invokes an installed coding tool (Amp or Claude Code); fresh worker instances get state via git history, progress.txt and prd.md.

name: gastown
pass5_evidence: Multi-agent workspace manager that orchestrates Claude, Gemini, Codex, Cursor, Amp, OpenCode, Copilot and others through tmux, assigning roles and managing session lifecycle.

name: Paseo
pass5_evidence: Local daemon that manages Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode and Pi sessions: creates workspaces/worktrees, launches provider processes, sends prompts and follow-ups, schedules heartbeats.

name: Superset
pass5_evidence: 'Any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Amp, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, and more, or the built-in chat.' Superset supplies isolated git worktrees so many agents run in parallel; the external agents do the coding.
review_flag: Not to be confused with Apache Superset (BI tool); this is superset.sh.

name: humanlayer
pass5_evidence: Sessions are 'one conversation with a coding agent' with configurable agent and model settings; docs include 'Set up Codex CLI' and Claude via AWS Bedrock. HumanLayer starts and manages the session; the coding agent edits files.

name: Agent Orchestrator (AO)
pass5_evidence: 'Agent IDE that enables you to manage fleets of coding agents' with an agentic orchestrator that plans tasks and spawns agents; the README states agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code and OpenCode still do the coding.

name: Omnigent
pass5_evidence: Self-described 'open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents - swap harnesses without rewrites'. Installs and launches those runtimes.

name: Claude Squad
pass5_evidence: 'Manage multiple AI terminal agents like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Amp' in separate tmux sessions and git worktrees; creates/pauses/resumes sessions and previews diffs.

name: yao
pass5_evidence: Current identity is 'Yao Agents': agents run on your own devices, every machine is another place for them to work, 'all managed from one place', isolated workspaces, a task board, and an integrated DeepSeek Harness usable from desktop/browser. Primary role is launching and managing agent sessions across nodes.
lifecycle_finding: Repositioned from a general single-binary app runtime to a self-hosted agent/workspace manager.
review_flag: CHANGE support->multiplexer (restores original label). Pass 4's 'general AI/app runtime' reading is stale - the current README is entirely about managing agents and workspaces. Medium confidence: the agents are general-purpose, not exclusively coding agents.

name: Xcode Coding Intelligence
pass5_evidence: Xcode 26.3 added agentic coding via installable providers - Claude Agent and Codex are configured in Settings > Intelligence, and native MCP support lets any compatible agent use Xcode's ~20 built-in tools. Xcode 26.6 adds Agent Client Protocol so any ACP agent can plug into the Intelligence panel. Xcode hosts and supplies tools; the agent owns the loop.

name: Netlify AI
pass5_evidence: Docs list supported agents verbatim: 'Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini, OpenCode'. Netlify supplies project context, credentials, compute, deployment pipeline and previews; the selected agent does the coding.

name: Tembo
pass5_evidence: Docs state plainly: 'Tembo is harness and model agnostic. For each agent you configure, you pick the harness (and model) that runs in the session it spawns' - Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Opencode, Pi, Amp.

name: Niteshift
pass5_evidence: 'Niteshift clones your repository, runs your Niteshift setup script, boots your dev server, and starts the agent (Claude Code or Codex) inside the environment.' The selected agent edits files and runs commands.

Software Factory produces requirements, blueprints and work orders; 'Work Orders integrates with local development environments through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This enables coding agents like Cursor or Claude Code to pull Work Order details'. The user tells their own agent to fetch the next work order - 8090 never launches or manages the agent process.
review_flag: That distinction is what keeps it support rather than multiplexer.

name: coze-studio
pass5_evidence: All-in-one visual low/no-code platform for creating, debugging, publishing and deploying general AI agents, applications and workflows with prompts, RAG, plugins and knowledge bases. The user assembles an agent on it; the assembled agent, not Coze Studio, would own any loop.
lifecycle_finding: Active; ByteDance open-sourced it. Last push 2026-07-29.
review_flag: RULED BR-008 (2026-08-25): no-code agent-building platforms are support, matching every other agent framework in the census (CrewAI, AutoGen, AgentScope, Swarms, Qwen-Agent, LangChain, Flue). Resolves the consistency flag against ChatDev 2.0 - both now support.

name: video-use
pass5_evidence: A video-editing skill installed into Claude Code/Codex/other shell-capable agents; transcribes footage, has the host agent choose an edit decision list, renders with ffmpeg.
review_flag: MINOR FLAG: literally a skill that supports coding agents (which reads as support), but the work product is video, not software - hence something-else. Both prior passes agree; noted only for transparency.

name: Pentestgpt
pass5_evidence: Automated penetration-testing/CTF agentic framework with recon, exploitation and reporting stages. Its loop targets security testing, not software construction.
review_flag: It can drive Claude Code or Codex as pluggable backends, but the task domain is pentesting, so it stays outside the coding census.

name: learn-coding-agent
pass5_evidence: 'Research on Coding Agents' - an educational/research repository analysing Claude Code and CLI-agent architecture. No shipped runtime.

name: valuecell
pass5_evidence: Community-driven multi-agent platform for financial applications: research, stock selection, tracking and trading. No project-code creation.

name: electric
pass5_evidence: README is unambiguous: 'Electric is a Postgres sync engine ... a read-path sync engine for Postgres.' No agentic loop, no code modification.
lifecycle_finding: NOTE: docs domain moved - electric-sql.com/docs now redirects to electric.ax/docs/sync. The GitHub description markets it as 'The agent platform built on sync', which conflicts with the README's own definition.

name: InkOS
pass5_evidence: 'Story Creation AI Agent for novel, scripts, translation, interactive games, and IP content'. Owns creative-writing workflows, not software implementation.

name: FinRobot
pass5_evidence: Open-source AI agent platform for financial applications; a Lead Agent routes data, analysis, modelling, synthesis and reporting agents. Valuation code is internal, not user-project code.

name: GLM-5
pass5_evidence: A flagship foundation-model family repository (GLM-5/5.1/5.2). A model, not a harness - it can generate code only when embedded in a host.

name: AppAgent
pass5_evidence: LLM-based multimodal smartphone-use framework: observes screens, decides taps/swipes and operates installed mobile apps. No code writing.

name: OpenSpec
pass5_evidence: Spec-driven development framework and CLI for AI coding assistants; OpenSpec manages specs, plans and indexes while the host assistant does planning and implementation.

name: BMAD-METHOD
pass5_evidence: An installed method, agent-role set and workflow system for AI-driven development; users invoke it inside an existing AI coding tool, which owns inference and tools.

name: ai-website-cloner-template
pass5_evidence: 'Clone any website with one command using AI coding agents' - a template of skills, commands, rules, scripts and a Next.js starter. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini executes the workflow.

name: agents.md
pass5_evidence: sdsrss/agentsmd is an AGENTS.md coding-discipline spec plus a native-hooks plugin for OpenAI Codex CLI; Codex owns the task loop.
lifecycle_finding: Real but very obscure: 0 stars, created recently (pushed 2026-08-20).
review_flag: IDENTITY FLAG: category is support either way, but 'agents.md' most commonly denotes the cross-vendor AGENTS.md open standard (agents.md), not this 0-star Codex plugin. Worth confirming the census row points at the intended artifact.

name: OpenCodeReview
pass5_evidence: Alibaba's hybrid code-review tool: deterministic pipelines plus an LLM review agent producing line-level findings. Output is review comments, not a general implementation loop.

name: Hindsight

name: agency-agents-zh
pass5_evidence: A Chinese community library of 267 plug-and-play AI expert roles supporting 18 host tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Hermes Agent and others). The host executes the installed roles.

name: sealos
pass5_evidence: AI-native Kubernetes cloud OS with Devbox, databases and deployment: 'Deploy real projects from GitHub or your AI coding agent, then keep them running'. Provisions environments; IDE/coding agents author the software.

name: LangChain JS Tools
pass5_evidence: JavaScript framework primitives for defining callable tools; the application's chat model/agent decides when to call them. Tools execute code only if a developer supplies such a function.

name: OpenWiki
pass5_evidence: 'A CLI that writes and maintains agent documentation for your codebase.' It authors and updates docs/wikis, not project implementation code.

name: GitIngest
pass5_evidence: Turns a Git repository into a prompt-friendly text digest for feeding into an LLM. No loop, no code modification.
lifecycle_finding: Live - gitingest.com serves normally (an earlier curl failure was bot-blocking, not an outage).

name: context-hub
pass5_evidence: Curated, versioned docs plus a chub CLI, explicitly 'designed for your coding agent to use (not for you to use!)'. The calling agent reads and applies the docs; Context Hub writes only local annotations.

name: context-engineering-intro
pass5_evidence: A context-engineering template of rules, examples, feature-request files and PRP commands; Claude Code or another assistant runs generate-prp / execute-prp and implements.

name: InsForge
pass5_evidence: 'The all-in-one, open-source backend platform for agentic coding. InsForge gives your coding agent database, auth, storage, compute, hosting, and AI gateway.' External MCP-compatible agents decide and execute; InsForge mutates backend resources.

name: PR-Agent
pass5_evidence: AI PR reviewer with describe/review/improve/ask/changelog commands; output is descriptions, findings and suggestions rather than an owned implementation loop.
lifecycle_finding: Now community-maintained at The-PR-Agent/pr-agent, donated by Qodo and explicitly 'not the Qodo free tier'.

name: Smol Developer

review_flag: BORDERLINE harness/support: it does create code, but does not own an autonomous act-observe-continue loop.

name: OpenCodex
pass5_evidence: 'Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code' - a local provider/protocol proxy and account router. Host clients keep session orchestration, tools and code edits; OpenCodex translates requests.

name: Yeoman
pass5_evidence: Deterministic scaffolding generator framework and CLI ecosystem; generator methods run in a predefined order. No agentic loop.
lifecycle_finding: Effectively dormant - umbrella repo last push 2022-10-18, though docs remain available.

name: Graphql-Playground
pass5_evidence: A GraphQL IDE for interactive queries, docs and subscriptions. No LLM, no agentic loop, no coding-agent support role.
lifecycle_finding: Repository ARCHIVED 2026-05-04; development moved to GraphiQL.

name: TypeChat
